question: Will Angie Nixon be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Florida?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Florida.

If no 2026 Florida Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Florida Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: The Senate seat at stake in this year’s election demands someone willing and prepared to address the issues Floridians actually live with: housing costs, insurance, health care, wages, child care, election integrity and government accountability. By that measure, The Miami Times endorses candidate Angie Nixon.

Two Democrats are looking to unseat U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Florida, in November, but they have to get through the primary race first. State Rep. Angie Nixon, D-Jacksonville, is a progressive lawmaker. Alex Vindman is a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel.

evidence.publisher: Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate — campaign press release
evidence.excerpt: Today, Common Defense, a leading national grassroots organization of veterans and military families, announced it is endorsing State Representative Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate in Florida. Rep. Nixon’s endorsements also include Congressman Maxwell Frost, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, civil rights attorney Ben Crump, former Ohio State Senator Nina Turner, former Congressman Al Lawson, and former Congressman Jamaal Bowman.

There’s been little public polling between the two Democrats as the primary nears. A big point of contention is that Vindman has avoided a debate with Nixon, much to her disappointment. One of Vindman’s most remarkable feats as a candidate to date has been his ability to raise money — more than $19 million since getting into the race in January, more than anyone else in the contest.

The poll shows Moody up over Nixon, 50%-42%. Moody leads Vindman, 50%-40%. Vindman has reported raising $16.7 million. Nixon has reported raising a little more than $625,000, with approximately $118,000 cash on hand at the end of June.

The campaign was asked about internal polling in the Primary race, but did not provide even a topline during the availability. A Change Research poll released Thursday sheds some light though, showing Vindman up 34% to 24%, with 41% of Democrats undecided.

evidence.publisher: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections
evidence.excerpt: The Florida Division of Elections calendar lists Primary Election Day as August 18, 2026. It lists mandatory early voting for August 8–15, 2026, and the voter-registration deadline as July 20, 2026.
